public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 487

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/487](https://www.erdosproblems.com/487)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta Arithmetica
  (1936), 147-151.
- [Kl71] Kleitman, Daniel, *Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union*.
  Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos487

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have positive density. Must there exist distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such
that $[a,b]=c$ (where $[a,b]$ is the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$)?

This is true, a consequence of the positive solution to [447] by Kleitman [Kl71].

Davenport and Erdős [DaEr36] showed that there must exist an infinite sequence $a_1<a_2\cdots$
in $A$ such that $a_i\mid a_j$ for all $i\leq j$, under the assumption that the upper logarithmic
density of $A$ is positive.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos487.lean"]
theorem erdos_487 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.HasPosDensity →
      ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c ∧ Nat.lcm a b = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos487

findings.description:
The hypothesis `A.HasPosDensity` (`∃ α > 0, A.HasDensity α`) requires the natural density of A to exist and be positive. That is the literal reading of the erdosproblems.com wording "positive density". Under it the Lean statement is true and correctly tagged (see notes). But in the hypothesis of a statement quantified over all A, it is the weakest possible reading.

Erdős's own precise formulation, in the cited [Er65b], poses the conjecture for sequences of positive LOWER density. A set of positive lower density need not have a density. It need not even contain a subset that has a positive density. Example: A = ⋃_k [4^k, 2·4^k) has lower density 1/3. Any B ⊆ A has no elements in [2·4^k, 4^{k+1}), so if B had density β, then β = 2β and β = 0. So `∀ A, 0 < A.lowerDensity → ∃ triple` is not a formal consequence of the Lean right-hand side. The Lean states only a special case of the problem as Erdős posed it.

The positive-upper-density reading is not an option. Besicovitch's primitive sets have positive upper density and contain no lcm-triple, because a | lcm(a,b) = c. That reading would contradict the source's "This is true". So lower density is the only precise reading that is both stronger and true.

The stronger version costs nothing. The linked proof (plby, `Erdos487.erdos_487`) proves exactly it, with hypothesis liminf |A∩[1,N]|/N > 0. I compiled its current port (textually identical theorem statement) against the local Mathlib. From it I derived, with only standard axioms, both the file's statement and `True ↔ ∀ A : Set ℕ, 0 < A.lowerDensity → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c ∧ Nat.lcm a b = c`, using the repository's own `Set.lowerDensity`.

The repository's own docstrings describe positive lower density as what Erdős' "positive density" "usually abbreviates" (470). They also say that `HasPosDensity` in a hypothesis claims less than that reading (318). Against this, the literal wording on erdosproblems.com and in [Er61] supports the current choice. That is why this is questionable rather than a misformalization.
findings.source_evidence:
erdosproblems.com/487 (LaTeX source, fetched via https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/487): "Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have positive density. Must there exist distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that $[a,b]=c$ ... This is true, a consequence of the positive solution to [447] by Kleitman".

[Er65b] Erdős, Some recent advances and current problems in number theory, p. 228 (scan at https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-17.pdf): "Davenport and I [45] proved that if a_1 < ... is an infinite sequence of positive lower density then there exists an infinite subsequence ... satisfying a_{i_j} | a_{i_{j+1}}. I conjectured that there are infinitely many triples a_i, a_j, a_l of distinct integers of the sequence satisfying [a_i, a_j] = a_l. This would follow from the following purely combinatorial theorem ... f(n) = o(2^n)."

[Er61] problem I.26, p. 236 (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1961-22.pdf): "if a_1, a_2, ... is a sequence of positive density, we can select an infinite subsequence ... It is an open problem if three distinct a's exist satisfying [a_i, a_j] = a_r." Here Erdős's "positive density" is loose shorthand: DaEr36 proves the divisibility-chain result under positive upper logarithmic density.
findings.suggested_fix:
theorem erdos_487 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, 0 < A.lowerDensity →
      ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c ∧ Nat.lcm a b = c

Keep the current natural-density statement as `erdos_487.variants.natural_density`. Add a docstring sentence citing [Er65b] ("positive lower density") for the reading. The existing `formal_proof` link proves both statements.

reformulations.difference: The Lean asks for one lcm-triple of distinct elements, as erdosproblems.com/487 does. [Er65b] and the remark on erdosproblems.com/447 ask for infinitely many triples.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Take a set A of positive density with only finitely many triples. Remove the finitely many elements that occur in them. The density is unchanged, so the one-triple statement gives a triple in the smaller set. That triple is also a triple of A, so its elements were removed: contradiction. The converse is trivial. Proved in /workspace/review/scratch3.lean as `Review.exists_iff_infinite` (via `hasDensity_diff_finite`), using only standard axioms. The same argument works for lower density.

review.notes:
The file has one declaration. Its statement, docstring, category, answer and `formal_proof` record all agree with erdosproblems.com/487. The docstring reproduces the site's LaTeX source verbatim. The site's status is "PROVED (LEAN)", and the teorth database says "proved (Lean)", last update 2026-02-16. So `research solved`, `answer(True)` and `formal_proof using lean4` are all current, and there are no status issues.

Checks done in Lean (scratch files in /workspace/review):
- The statement elaborates as `True ↔ ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.HasPosDensity → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c ∧ a.lcm b = c`.
- The hypothesis is satisfiable (`Set.univ`), so the statement is not vacuous.
- 0 can never occur in a valid triple, because lcm(0, b) = 0 forces a repeated element. So allowing 0 ∈ A is harmless.

The `formal_proof` link is a stable commit link, and neither linked file (Erdos487, Erdos447) contains `sorry` or axioms. The cited v4.29.1 file does not match the local toolchain (v4.33.1), so I did not compile it. Instead I compiled the plby "latest" (v4.33.0) port of Erdos447 and Erdos487 against the local Mathlib. Its `erdos_487` statement and `lowerDensity` definition are textually identical to the cited file's. Both compile with no errors and depend only on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

Importing that build together with FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Data.Set.Density, I derived the file's exact statement (scratch4.lean, `Review.fc_erdos_487`). I also derived its lower-density strengthening (scratch5.lean, `Review.fc_erdos_487_lower`). Both depend only on standard axioms.

The single finding is a judgement call on how to read "positive density", graded honestly as questionable.

Access notes: erdosproblems.com refused every curl User-Agent (Cloudflare 403), and the Wayback Machine and Common Crawl were unreachable. I read the site through the r.jina.ai proxy. I read [Er61], [Er65b] and [DaEr36] from the OCR text layers of the Rényi Institute scans. The quoted passages are unambiguous despite OCR noise.
